subject.title: fix(agents): skip error classification for clean non-zero exits

question: Should OpenClaw preserve shell exit-code failure semantics by default and require an explicit accepted-exit signal, or redefine every normally terminated non-zero command as non-failing for channel warnings?
rationale: The runtime's `completed` status describes process termination, while whether a specific non-zero code is benign is command-dependent; source inspection cannot safely choose that user-facing warning policy without maintainer intent.

options.title: Require explicit accepted exits
options.body: Keep non-zero exits warning by default and add or use a narrow owner-level signal only when the command intentionally accepts particular exit codes.

options.title: Suppress all completed non-zero exits
options.body: Adopt the PR's broad interpretation and intentionally accept that normally terminated command failures will no longer produce tool-error warnings.

recommendation.title: Require explicit accepted exits
recommendation.body: Keep non-zero exits warning by default and add or use a narrow owner-level signal only when the command intentionally accepts particular exit codes.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is prior work establishing user-visible tool-failure warning behavior in this agent path.
